data.name: T cell differentiation
data.description: Process by which immune T cells commit to effector versus regulatory fates; directly controlled by mTOR complex activity.
data.description_beginner: How immune T cells decide what kind of cell to become - an attacking (effector) cell or a peacekeeping (regulatory) cell. mTOR activity is one of the switches that helps make this decision.

studies.title: Enforcing mTORC1 activity in therapeutic CD4+ T cells promotes persistence but eventual immune exhaustion
studies.authors: Sillito F; Armbrecht E; O'Neill AT; McIntyre A; Nyatondo M; Holler A; Callender LA; Henson SM; Stauss H; Chakraverty R

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse CD4+ T cells, adoptive transfer tumor model
studies.finding: Enforced RHEB overexpression (mTORC1 hyperactivation) in therapeutic CD4+ T cells boosts initial proliferation/persistence after adoptive transfer, but drives cells toward an exhausted phenotype (co-inhibitory receptors, impaired re-proliferation on rechallenge) -- a double-edged sword for CAR/TCR-T cell engineering, distinct from the CD8 response to the same manipulation.

studies.title: Amino acid homeostasis by CORVET/HOPS: A metabolic and stress resilience checkpoint for T cells
studies.authors: Wang J; Ni Z; Zhang Xinxin; He L; Cheng X; Huang L; Ye H; Li P; Zhao TJ; Du X
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse T cells (conditional VPS18 / VPS11 knockout, in vitro and in vivo)
studies.finding: Identifies the CORVET and HOPS endolysosomal tethering complexes as upstream suppliers of intracellular amino acids in activated T cells, acquired via macropinocytosis. Loss of the core subunits VPS18 or VPS11 starves the cell of amino acids, switches on the integrated stress response and shuts down mTORC1; enforced mTORC1 activity rescues the proliferative defect while BIM deletion rescues survival, separating the two failure modes. Places vesicular nutrient acquisition upstream of the canonical lysosomal amino-acid-sensing arm of mTORC1.

studies.title: TCR-mTORC1 signaling promotes epigenetic stabilization of Foxp3 expression in regulatory T cells via TET protein translation
studies.authors: Kinoshita T; Nakajima A; Kobayashi T; Ohno M; Wei Y; Hasegawa T; Hayatsu N; Hirayama S; Tsukada YI; Hirao A; Murata S; Hori S
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse; in vitro-induced regulatory T cells (iTreg)
studies.finding: Sustained TCR signaling activates mTORC1, which boosts translation of the TET2 (and likely TET3) DNA-demethylation enzymes; this demethylates the Foxp3 TSDR enhancer and epigenetically locks in stable Foxp3 expression in regulatory T cells. In vivo mTORC1 inactivation increases methylated-TSDR Foxp3+ T cells, confirming the pathway's physiological relevance.

studies.title: The role of mTORC2/RICTOR in immune cells and inflammatory diseases.
studies.authors: Xu J; Zhong W; Xin F; Xu F; Zheng Z; Guo F

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Review of immune cell subsets (T cells, B cells, macrophages, dendritic cells, NK cells) and mouse conditional-knockout models
studies.finding: mTORC2/RICTOR signaling (via AKT, SGK1, PKC) shapes Th1/Th2 differentiation, Treg stability, memory T cell formation, BCR signaling and plasma cell survival, and macrophage/DC/NK function; its role in tissue inflammation is context-dependent (exacerbating osteoarthritis and pancreatitis but restraining pro-inflammatory polarization in colorectal cancer), and dual mTORC1/2 inhibitors (e.g. AZD2014) show early but complicated promise.

studies.title: Enhancing CD8 T-cell memory by modulating fatty acid metabolism
studies.authors: Pearce EL; Walsh MC; Cejas PJ; Harms GM; Shen H; Wang LS; Jones RG; Choi Y

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mice with T-cell-specific TRAF6 deletion (CD4-cre), OT-I TCR-transgenic adoptive transfer, Listeria monocytogenes-OVA infection, EL4-OVA tumour vaccine model, and activated mouse CD8 T cells in vitro after IL-2 withdrawal
studies.finding: Mice whose T cells lacked the adaptor protein TRAF6 mounted a normal effector CD8 T-cell response to Listeria infection, but the antigen-specific cells vanished during contraction and almost no memory cells formed. The TRAF6-deficient cells failed to activate AMPK and mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation when the growth factor IL-2 was withdrawn. Daily metformin restored fatty acid oxidation and memory formation, and also raised memory CD8 T-cell numbers in normal mice: in a tumour vaccine model 6 of 9 metformin-treated mice survived beyond day 33 against 1 of 8 controls. Daily rapamycin (1.5 mg/kg), used as a second drug that promotes fatty acid oxidation, likewise increased memory CD8 T-cell development and recall responses. Boundary: mouse only, one bacterial infection model and one transplantable tumour; the rapamycin arm is a secondary experiment and mTOR activity itself was not measured in these cells.

studies.title: The mTOR kinase determines effector versus memory CD8+ T cell fate by regulating the expression of transcription factors T-bet and Eomesodermin
studies.authors: Rao RR; Li Q; Odunsi K; Shrikant PA

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Naive mouse OT-I CD8 T cells (and STAT4-deficient OT-I) stimulated in vitro with antigen plus B7.1 and IL-12, with rapamycin, PI3K inhibition, insulin or 2-deoxyglucose; adoptive transfer into C57BL/6 recipients and E.G7 tumour challenge
studies.finding: Working with naive OT-I CD8 T cells stimulated by antigen plus B7.1, the authors showed that IL-12 both raised and prolonged mTOR phosphorylation and S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation out to 48 hours, and that this required PI3K throughout and STAT4 for the late phase. Rapamycin, added at the start or only at 12 hours, blocked the sustained expression of T-bet and with it the heritable type I effector programme, while raising Eomesodermin and producing cells with a memory-precursor phenotype (CD62L high, KLRG1 low, Bcl-2 high). Restoring T-bet by a tamoxifen-inducible construct brought back IFN-gamma production and lowered Eomesodermin, which places T-bet downstream of mTOR in this system. After transfer, the rapamycin-treated cells persisted better, gave stronger antigen-recall responses, and more than 78 percent of recipients stayed tumour-free to day 120 against 50 percent fatality with IL-12-conditioned effector cells. Boundary: mouse CD8 T cells, one TCR-transgenic system with pharmacological mTOR inhibition in vitro before transfer; the transplantable E.G7 tumour is a model, not a treatment result in people, and the memory-precursor phenotype faded by day 40 after transfer.

studies.title: Cutting edge: distinct glycolytic and lipid oxidative metabolic programs are essential for effector and regulatory CD4+ T cell subsets
studies.authors: Michalek RD; Gerriets VA; Jacobs SR; Macintyre AN; MacIver NJ; Mason EF; Sullivan SA; Nichols AG; Rathmell JC

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Primary mouse CD4 T cells polarised in vitro to Th1, Th2, Th17 and inducible Treg, with rapamycin, metformin or the CPT1 inhibitor etomoxir; Glut1-transgenic and Glut1-myc knock-in mice; OVA-driven allergic asthma model with metformin
studies.finding: Comparing CD4 T cells grown under effector and regulatory conditions, the authors showed that Th1, Th2 and Th17 cells carry high surface Glut1 and are strongly glycolytic, while inducible Treg carry little Glut1, oxidise lipid at a higher rate and have more phosphorylated AMPK. Blocking lipid oxidation with etomoxir selectively suppressed Treg generation and left effector differentiation intact, whereas removing glucose blocked Th17 but not Treg. Both rapamycin and metformin raised fatty acid oxidation in stimulated CD4 T cells, and etomoxir prevented the Treg increase produced by rapamycin or TGF-beta, which ties the pro-Treg effect of mTOR inhibition to lipid oxidation. In a mouse asthma model, metformin lowered Glut1 on activated CD4 T cells and increased the proportion and number of Treg in draining lymph nodes, although airway responsiveness itself did not change significantly. Boundary: mouse cells and one mouse allergic-airway model; mTOR inhibition is pharmacological (rapamycin) and mTOR activity was not measured directly, so the mTOR arm is inferred from drug effects.

studies.title: mTORC1 and mTORC2 selectively regulate CD8+ T cell differentiation
studies.authors: Pollizzi KN; Patel CH; Sun IH; Oh MH; Waickman AT; Wen J; Delgoffe GM; Powell JD

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mice with T-cell-specific deletion of Tsc2, Rheb or Rictor (and Tsc2/Rictor double knockout), OT-I adoptive transfer, vaccinia-OVA and Listeria-OVA infection, EL4 and B16-OVA tumour models, rapamycin (100 ug/kg/day) and 2-deoxyglucose in vivo, Seahorse metabolic profiling
studies.finding: By deleting Tsc2, Rheb or Rictor in T cells, this work split the CD8 response between the two mTOR complexes. Tsc2 loss left mTORC1 constitutively active: the cells were strongly glycolytic (high ECAR, high Slc2a1 and Pfk1, low spare respiratory capacity), made more IFN-gamma, TNF and granzyme B, cleared EL4 thymoma and slowed B16-OVA growth, but stayed terminally differentiated and were about two-fold fewer than wild type at day 30, with no memory. Rheb loss removed mTORC1 activity with mTORC2 intact: those cells failed as effectors but kept memory-like features and were about two-fold more numerous at day 30, yet did not respond to rechallenge, which the authors trace to metabolic defects. Rapamycin from day 5 (100 ug/kg daily) rescued survival of Tsc2-deficient cells, raised CD127 and Eomesodermin, lowered KLRG1 and T-bet and restored a recall response. Losing mTORC2 by Rictor deletion left effector function intact but increased memory cells that still responded 133 days after infection, and the Tsc2/Rictor double knockout showed that the hyperactive effector phenotype needs mTORC2. Boundary: mouse genetics with TCR-transgenic transfers and transplantable tumours; the comparison rests on genetic extremes (no TSC2, no Rheb, no Rictor) rather than graded physiological signalling, and nothing here is measured in people.

studies.title: L-Arginine Modulates T Cell Metabolism and Enhances Survival and Anti-tumor Activity
studies.authors: Geiger R; Rieckmann JC; Wolf T; Basso C; Feng Y; Fuhrer T; Kogadeeva M; Picotti P; Meissner F; Mann M; Zamboni N; Sallusto F; Lanzavecchia A

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human primary naive CD4 and CD8 T cells with high-resolution metabolomics, proteomics and limited-proteolysis mass spectrometry, plus CRISPR knockout T-cell clones; mouse HA-TCR transgenic transfers with oral L-arginine, and B16-OVA melanoma with OT-I transfer
studies.finding: Tracking metabolites and proteins in activated human T cells, the authors found intracellular L-arginine falls sharply after activation even in 1 mM medium, because uptake and conversion to ornithine, proline and spermidine rise. Raising L-arginine shifted metabolism from glycolysis towards oxidative phosphorylation, increased oxygen consumption and spare respiratory capacity, and produced central-memory-like cells (CCR7 and CD62L high, less IFN-gamma) with greater survival capacity; blocking arginase gave the same survival gain at physiological 150 uM L-arginine. Limited-proteolysis mass spectrometry plus knockout clones identified three nuclear proteins, BAZ1B, PSIP1 and TSN, that sense L-arginine and contribute to the survival programme. In mice, oral L-arginine raised serum levels from about 160 uM to 700 uM and roughly doubled intracellular L-arginine in activated T cells, and L-arginine-treated OT-I cells slowed B16-OVA growth and extended survival. The authors report explicitly that the survival effect was independent of mTOR: L-arginine did not change S6K1 or 4E-BP phosphorylation, and rapamycin, while also improving survival, changed metabolism in an entirely different way. Boundary: mostly human T cells in culture plus mouse transfer and transplantable-tumour models; the dietary arm is a mouse supplementation experiment, not a human trial, and mTOR enters only as a negative control.
